subject: Discovery recap: reliability & graceful degradation for Acme - next steps
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Jensen <sarah.jensen@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / reliability notes for Redwood POC

Thanks for the intro earlier 

I appreciate you taking the time. Quick recap from our side so we

we

're aligned before next steps.

Pain points:
- Latency spikes on our payment routing path during high load (2x spikes last quarter causing timeouts for downstream services).
- No reliable cross-region failover today; we saw a single-region outage that impacted ~30% of traffic for ~45 minutes.
- Current stack: custom embeddings service (vendor X), in-house model endpoints on AWS EC2/GPU, and an NGINX layer for routing.

Success criteria for a POC:
- 95th percentile generation latency < 200ms for our typical prompts
- Transparent fallback that reduces latency degradation under load (graceful degradation to smaller model + local cache)
- Clear cost estimates and observability (token-level cost, per-route latency)

Questions for Redwood:
- Can you outline your recommended fallback model strategy (variants + quantization) and cross-region failover options?
- What SLAs/SLOs do you offer on Dedicated vs Hosted?

I attached a small incident timeline that summarizes the recent outages. Happy to jump on another call to walk through the traces.

Thanks,
Tom
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Payments

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / reliability notes for Redwood POC

Tom

thanks for the clear recap and for sharing the incident timeline. Below is a short discovery recap and proposed next steps based on what you told us. Please flag anything we missed.

What we heard (pain points):
- Intermittent latency spikes and a single-region outage that should have failed over gracefully.
- Lack of automated model/region fallback and limited observability into token-level costs.
- Current stack includes vendor embeddings + self-hosted model endpoints (AWS).

Reliability & graceful degradation summary (Redwood approach):
- Fallback tiers: we recommend a 3-tier fallback profile for your workload:
  1) Primary: full-capacity model (quantized where possible) in primary region
  2) Secondary: smaller distilled variant for burst/failover traffic (lower latency, lower cost)
  3) Tertiary: cached responses / embeddings reuse + static templates for critical paths
- Cross-region routing: automatic smart routing with health checks and cold-start mitigation (warm-up policy + KV cache replication).
- SLO/SLA: Hosted API: best-effort SLOs (we'll share performance profiles); Dedicated: SLA-backed uptime and latency targets (can commit to 99.9% regional uptime and 95th pct latency targets in contract discussions).
- Observability: per-route token cost breakdown, per-request traces, and incident logs (we can ingest your traces).

POC proposal and success criteria:
- Duration: 4 weeks
- Objectives:
  • Validate 95th pct latency < 200ms under a representative load (we'll define a load profile together)
  • Demonstrate automated fallback to the secondary model with transparent degradation (user-facing latency increase capped)
  • Surface token-level cost estimates for your top 3 routes
- Deliverables: POC config, test plan, runbook for failover, and a short performance report.

Immediate next steps:
1) Share a representative prompt set and sample traffic (anonymized)  

— Marissa can coordinate the ingest.
2) Tech deep-dive with SREs/ML infra (30-45m) 

3) We'll provision a short-lived Dedicated trial environment and provide SOC2 summary and security docs (attached).

CC'ing Marissa to own the technical checklist and test-plan.

Thanks 

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: RDW-SOC2-summary.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro / reliability notes for Redwood POC

Tom 

quick technical notes to add to Ben's recap and to make the POC plan more concrete.

Fallback / degradation details:
- Model variants: we typically run an 8-bit quantized primary and an even smaller distilled float16 variant for failover. The distilled variant gives ~2-3x lower inference latency at ~10-15% quality delta depending on prompt.
- Cache strategy: prefix/KV cache for recent dialogs + embeddings cache for reranking. For payment routing, we recommend a KV policy with 30-60s TTL for high-frequency tokens to avoid repeated recomputation.
- Cross-region warm-up: replicate small subset of KV cache + async cold-start pre-warming (we can replay a small sample of traffic to the DR region before failover window).

Test plan outline for POC:
1) Define traffic profile (QPS, typical prompt length, 90/95/99 percentiles) 

2) Baseline measurement on your current endpoints (we'll script against your test harness).
3) Inject controlled failover scenarios (region outage, model OOM, heavy spike) and measure recovery time and degradation curve.
4) Cost modeling: run synthetic workload across models to estimate token-level unit economics.

Can you provide:
- A sanitized 48h traffic dump or the top 100 prompts and average token lengths
- Contact for procurement/finance to speed up Dedicated trial if this looks good

I attached a short fallback playbook with runbook steps we'll execute during the POC. I

I


— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
